I use Vim as my pager for man pages and Git. You can set it up by putting the following in your ~/.bashrc. I use Ubuntu Linux. Other distributions may not include macros/less.vim with Vim.

# Use vim as the pager for commands like `git log` and `git diff`. This gives
# syntax highlighting and code folding.
export GIT_PAGER="vim - -R -c 'set filetype=git' -c 'set foldmethod=syntax'"


# Use vim as the pager for man pages instead of the default, less.
#
# This makes vim act a LOT like less. See
# /usr/share/vim/vimcurrent/macros/less.vim for full details.
#
# The `col -b` strips our the extra backspace characters vim can't deal with.
# More details on this blogpost:
# [http://zameermanji.com/blog/2012/12/30/using-vim-as-manpager/](http://zameermanji.com/blog/2012/12/30/using-vim-as-manpager/)
# …and this Reddit discusion has some fixes for the blogpost:
# [http://www.reddit.com/r/vim/comments/15qad8/using_vim_as_manpager/](http://www.reddit.com/r/vim/comments/15qad8/using_vim_as_manpager/)
export MANPAGER="/bin/sh -c \"col -b | vim -R -c 'set filetype=man' -c 'runtime! macros/less.vim' -c ':set nonumber' -c ':set norelativenumber' -c ':set nocursorline' -\""
